how: Kept by hand. Clubs, sessions and races were read on 23 Nov 2026 from the organisers' own registration pages (runsignup.com), Go To Bermuda event listings, Bernews, The Royal Gazette and the World Triathlon site, the clubs' own websites, the PGA TOUR site and amateurgolf.com. Only what those pages say is here. Most 2027 calendars were not yet published, so past races are listed as the usual calendar with their 2025 or 2026 dates. Add each new season when it is announced and move review_after on. An event with an 'end' date drops into the usual calendar once that date has passed. Dance, CrossFit and gyms were added on 23 Nov 2026 from each studio's or gym's own website. Where a timetable sits inside a booking system the Hub links to it and lists no times. Facebook pages could not be read.

sports.name: Running
sports.lead: There is a race or a group run almost every week. Here is the calendar, the clubs and the big weekend in January.

bodies.name: Bermuda National Athletics Association
bodies.what: The national body. Listed as organiser of the Chubb Bermuda Triangle Challenge.

bodies.name: Mid Atlantic Athletic Club
bodies.what: One of the island's biggest running clubs, formed in June 1977. Members train together at the Tuesday social run and Wednesday track, with yoga and strength classes too. It puts on its own races, such as the No Frills 5K and 10K at Clearwater Beach each September, and members get 10% off Triangle Challenge entries. MAAC Juniors coaches runners aged 7 to 18 through the school year.

bodies.name: Grateful Miles Run Club
bodies.what: A community run club for all levels, with a group run every Sunday.

bodies.name: Swans Running Club
bodies.what: Formed in 1982 and named for Raymond Swan, its first president and one of Bermuda's best marathon runners. It meets every Tuesday and Thursday night and puts on several races a year, among them the Labour Day 5K, a charity run in October and the Turkey Trot in late November.

bodies.name: Race Day World
bodies.what: Not a club but the island's race calendar, entry desk and results service. Most local runs, walks, triathlons and swims are listed there.

sessions.what: A road race somewhere on the island
sessions.where: A different parish each week
sessions.note: In autumn 2026 there was a 5K or 10K on nearly every Sunday. Race Day World lists them all and takes the entries.

sessions.where: Hamilton
sessions.note: Three to five miles at your own pace, running or walking. Guests and visitors are welcome: just show up. On the last Tuesday of the month there are tacos afterwards at the Bermuda Bistro at the Beach, 105 Front Street.

sessions.where: National Sports Centre, Devonshire
sessions.note: Coached track sessions. The autumn block runs from 14 October 2026 to 13 January 2027 and builds to the marathon weekend. A spring block builds to the Bermuda Day half marathon. Sign up through Race Day World.

sessions.where: Ask the club for the meeting place
sessions.note: The club meets twice a week for running and walking.

sessions.where: A different start each week
sessions.note: All levels. Listed weekly until 21 March 2027.

events.name: Swans Running Club Turkey Trot
note: With Northshore Medical.

events.name: Red Cross Jingle Bell Run and Walk
note: The Christmas one.

events.name: Chubb Bermuda Triangle Challenge
events.where: Hamilton, the National Sports Centre and Dockyard
note: Three races in three days. Friday 7pm: the Butterfield Mile on Front Street. Saturday 9am: the Allshores 10K at the National Sports Centre, with a 5K run at 9:05 and a 5K walk at 9:10. Sunday 7am: the PwC Bermuda Marathon and Half Marathon.
2027 is the 50th running of the marathon.
The full challenge is the mile, the 10K and the marathon. The half challenge swaps in the half marathon.
Pasta dinner on Saturday 16 January, 6 to 8pm at the Hamilton Princess, $50, with Dame Flora Duffy as guest speaker.

events.name: Bermuda Connection 5K and 10K
note: $40 for the 5K, $50 for the 10K.

events.name: Cambridge Classic 5K and 10K Run and Walk
Rum to the Beach
note: A 7.13 mile race that many use as a warm up for the Triangle Challenge.

events.name: MAAC No Frills 5K and 10K
events.where: Clearwater Beach car park, St David's
note: Run by the Mid Atlantic Athletic Club.

events.name: The autumn Sundays
note: In 2026: the PartnerRe Women's 5K on 4 October, the Swans charity run on 18 October, the BNG Run for the Arts 5K on 25 October, the InEvo Re 10K on 1 November and the AXA XL Man on the Run 5K on 8 November.

events.name: The Legends Series and Bermuda Day
note: Late winter brings the older named races, among them the Ed Sherlock 8K and the Ludwig Cann 10K in February and Lindo's to Lindo's. The Bermuda Day Half Marathon Derby from Somerset is the one the whole island turns out to watch.

sports.source_note: Calendar from Race Day World, read on 23 November 2026.

sports.name: Cycling
sports.lead: Road racing with the association, and mountain biking with the Fat Tire Massive series through the winter.

bodies.name: Bermuda Bicycle Association
bodies.what: Founded in 1974. It runs the road and mountain bike race calendar, promotes Cycling for All club rides, develops junior riders and sends teams overseas. You must be a member to race: join through racedayworld.com.

bodies.name: Fat Tire Massive
bodies.what: The island's mountain bike racing series, seven races from October to April in parks from Dockyard to St David's. The master schedule is on its own website.

sessions.where: Various
sessions.note: The association promotes open club rides, but I found no published times. Check its website or Facebook page.

tips: A typical race morning starts with the juniors at about 8am, then the C category and women for 25 to 30 minutes, then the A and B categories for 35 to 40 minutes. Racing is usually over by 9:30 or 10am.
Adults usually pay $20 to $30 a race. Juniors often race free.

events.name: Fat Tire Massive mountain bike series, 2026 to 2027
note: Race 1, South Shore beach trails, 25 October. Race 2, Lagoon Park, 8 November. Race 3, Admiralty House, 29 November. Race 4, Great Head Park, 10 January. Race 5, Southlands, 7 February. Race 6, Ferry Reach Park, 14 March. Race 7, Little Head and Great Head Parks, 4 April.
$25 a race, or $125 for a pass to all seven. Bermuda Bicycle Association members get a discount.
Children of 8 and under ride free in the Pedal Palooza, short untimed loops with parents welcome to help.
Last season the open classes started at 9am and the novices and 13 to 16 year olds at 10:30am. Check the schedule for this year's times.

events.name: Round De Reach endurance race
note: Four hours on rough trails, solo or in teams.

events.name: President's Cup road race
events.where: From No. 1 Car Park, Front Street, Hamilton, 7:30am
note: About 54 miles. $30 for adults and $15 for juniors, for riders of racing age 15 and up.

events.name: Criterium races
events.where: Lamb Foggo and the Fort Knox loop in St David's, and Cross Island at Dockyard
note: Short circuit races, including the National Criterium Championships.

events.name: Individual and team time trials
events.where: Kindley Field Road, St David's, among others
note: Riders set off one at a time against the clock. Start times are sent out by email the day before.

sports.source_note: Mountain bike dates from the series entry page, read on 23 November 2026. The Round De Reach race date was not shown, only its entry deadline.

sports.name: Triathlon
sports.lead: The association, what you need to enter, and the races of the year.

bodies.name: Bermuda Triathlon Association
bodies.what: Runs the race calendar. Every competitor must be a member, and race entries include a $10 one day membership for those who are not. Join through racedayworld.com. Every race needs volunteers.

bodies.name: Race Day World
bodies.what: Lists the triathlons, duathlons and open water swims and takes the entries.

tips: Races are not draft legal: no riding in another rider's slipstream.
Juniors may use a mountain bike or a road bike.
No headphones while racing. Whether wetsuits are allowed depends on the water and air temperature on the day.

events.name: Cambridge Beaches Bermuda Triathlon
note: Swim, bike and run from the resort.

events.name: Americas Triathlon CARIFTA Championships
note: The regional junior championships, hosted in Bermuda in 2026. Sprint distance for the 17 to 21 age group: 750 metre swim, 20 km bike, 5 km run.

events.name: Olympic distance triathlon
note: With a team option.

events.name: National Sprint Triathlon Championships
note: Adult individual and team races, plus junior races.

events.name: Aon Mixed Team Relay National Championship
note: Short legs, with junior divisions from age 7.

events.name: Open water swims
note: Swimmers and triathletes share these: the open water national championships in September and the Round the Sound Swim in October (11 October in 2026).

sports.name: Sailing
sports.lead: The clubs, the weekly racing, and the regattas worth watching from shore.

bodies.name: Royal Bermuda Yacht Club
bodies.what: 15 Point Pleasant Road, Hamilton. Founded in 1844. Co-organiser of the Newport Bermuda Race and manager of the Antigua Bermuda Race, and a Royal Yachting Association training centre with learn to sail courses. It is free to walk down and look at the boats when a fleet is in.

bodies.name: Royal Hamilton Amateur Dinghy Club
bodies.what: Pomander Road, Paget. Founded in 1882 and the only dinghy club in the world with a royal title. Home to Bermuda's largest junior sailing fleet, with sailing lessons for juniors and adults all year, and the host of Wednesday Night Racing.

bodies.name: St George's Dinghy and Sports Club
bodies.what: On the waterfront of St George's Harbour. Home of the fitted dinghy Victory IV, and host of the opening day of the fitted dinghy season.

bodies.name: Sandys Boat Club
bodies.what: Mangrove Bay, Somerset. Home of the fitted dinghy Challenger II, christened in 1990.

bodies.name: Spanish Point Boat Club
bodies.what: Pembroke. Going since 1943.

bodies.name: West End Sailboat Club
bodies.what: Somerset. Founded in 1941 by a group of Somerset sailors and boat builders, and the home of the Edward Cross Long Distance Comet Race.

bodies.name: Mid Atlantic Boat and Sports Club
bodies.what: Founded in 1944. One of the three clubs that race Comets.

bodies.name: East End Mini Yacht Club
bodies.what: Convict Bay, St George's. Racing Comets since 1968, from the same building it started in.

bodies.name: Endeavour Community Sailing
bodies.what: The youth programme that grew out of the America's Cup. It teaches schoolchildren to sail from bases at each end of the island.

events.name: Bermuda fitted dinghy season
events.when: Late May to early September (the 2026 season opened on Sunday 24 May)
events.where: St George's Harbour, Hamilton Harbour, Granaway Deep and Mangrove Bay
note: Four boats race for their clubs: Contest III for the Royal Bermuda Yacht Club, Elizabeth II for the Royal Hamilton Amateur Dinghy Club, Victory IV for St George's and Challenger II for Sandys.
Opening day in 2026 had three races, at noon, 1:30pm and 3pm, in St George's Harbour.

events.name: Edward Cross Long Distance Comet Race
events.when: National Heroes Day weekend in June
note: Comets from the West End Sailboat Club, the Mid Atlantic Boat and Sports Club and the East End Mini Yacht Club race the length of the island for the Edward Cross Memorial Cup.

events.name: Marion Bermuda Race
events.when: June, every second year. The next starts on 18 June 2027
events.where: Finishes at the Royal Hamilton Amateur Dinghy Club
note: The 50th anniversary race, from Marion, Massachusetts. The fleet ties up at the dinghy club afterwards.

events.name: SailGP
note: The international foiling catamaran league is due back on the Great Sound in 2027.

events.name: Newport Bermuda Race
events.when: June, every second year (started 19 June in 2026)
note: 635 miles from Newport, Rhode Island, and one of the oldest ocean races in the world, first sailed in 1906. Run by the Cruising Club of America and the Royal Bermuda Yacht Club. The next one is due in 2028.

events.name: Antigua Bermuda Race
events.when: Late April into May (started 29 April in 2026)
note: About 935 nautical miles from Antigua, managed by the Royal Bermuda Yacht Club.

events.name: Bermuda International Invitational Race Week
note: A week of keelboat racing hosted by the Royal Bermuda Yacht Club.

events.name: Bermuda Gold Cup
note: Match racing in Hamilton Harbour.

sessions.when: Wednesdays, first start 6:05pm, late March to early September
sessions.where: Royal Hamilton Amateur Dinghy Club, Paget
sessions.note: The island's most popular midweek racing. The 2026 series ran from 25 March to 9 September and drew 41 boats from every local club. Ask the club's sailing office about crewing.

tips: A fitted dinghy is only 14 feet long but carries a huge spread of sail and a crew of six. Crews have been known to jump overboard mid race to lighten the boat.
Good places to watch fitted dinghy racing: the wharves on the St George's waterfront, and Mangrove Bay in Somerset.
Comet racing grew up in Bermuda's historically Black boat clubs in the 1940s, and the long distance race has been sailed since 1944.

sports.name: Power boats
sports.lead: The racing season, where to watch, and the Round the Island race.

bodies.name: Bermuda Power Boat Association
bodies.what: Runs the national championship season from May to September. Racing is free to watch from shore.

tips: Race days at Ferry Reach run between 10am and 5pm, and the water is closed to other boats and patrolled.
Round the Island is often postponed for weather. In 2025 it moved twice because of small craft warnings, so check on the morning.

events.name: Rubis Round the Island
events.when: August (9 August in 2026, with 16 and 23 August as backup dates)
note: The big one: the fleet races right round Bermuda. Free to watch from anywhere on the coast.

events.name: Ferry Reach races
events.when: May to September (the 2026 season opened here on 3 May and returned on 13 September)
note: Closed circuit racing close to shore.

events.name: Hamilton Harbour race
note: Closed circuit racing in front of the city.

events.name: St George's and Cross Island races
events.when: Through the season (St George's was 30 August in 2026)
note: The season also visits Cross Island at Dockyard and ended in 2026 with a race at Spanish Point Boat Club on 27 September.

sports.source_note: 2026 schedule from Bernews, 9 May 2026. The 2027 schedule was not out when this was written.

sports.name: Golf
sports.lead: Seven courses on 21 square miles. Pick one for its scorecard, rating and slope, signature hole and a map.

bodies.name: Bermuda Golf Association
bodies.what: The national body. It runs the national championships, which are open to its members and to visitors with a current handicap.

tips: Fees change with the season and the time of day, and some sources disagree, so treat the prices here as a guide and check with the course.
There is also an 18 hole mini golf course, Bermuda Fun Golf, at Dockyard.

events.name: Butterfield Bermuda Championship
note: Bermuda's PGA TOUR event, first played in 2019. It moved to October in 2026 from mid November the year before. Spectator tickets started at about $38.

events.name: Goslings Bermuda Open
note: The national open, 54 holes for professionals and low handicap amateurs. The winner earns a place in the Butterfield Bermuda Championship.

events.name: Bermuda Stroke Play Championship
note: The 54 hole national stroke play title.

events.name: Bermuda Match Play Championship
note: A stroke play qualifying round on the Friday, then match play on Saturday and Sunday, with men's and senior divisions.

events.name: Bermuda Ladies Pro-Am Golf Classic
events.when: March (8 to 14 March in 2026, the 27th year)
note: Up to 20 teams, each of one woman professional and three amateurs.

sports.source_note: Scorecards, ratings and slopes from GolfPass, 18Birdies and the Bermuda Tourism golf guide, read on 23 November 2026. Sources sometimes differ by a few yards or a slope point, and tees get moved, so the card in the pro shop is the one that counts. 2027 tournament dates were not out when this was written.

courses.name: Port Royal Golf Course
courses.what: The Government's championship course on the cliffs of the west end, and the home of Bermuda's PGA TOUR event, when it is stretched to 6,828 yards. Doglegs and wind are the defence. It shares playing privileges with Ocean View.
sig: Tee and green both sit on the edge of the cliff with the Atlantic below and to the left, and the wind decides the club. It is the most photographed hole in Bermuda and one of the most feared.
more: The 15th, a 401 yard par 4, is rated the hardest hole on the card, with the best view on the course.
The 11th, par 4, tumbles downhill toward the Great Sound.
The 7th, a par 5, drops off the tee, bends left and climbs steeply to the green.

courses.name: The Mid Ocean Club
courses.what: The classic. Charles Blair Macdonald laid it out with Seth Raynor in 1921, building in his versions of the great holes of Britain, and Robert Trent Jones Sr. revised it in 1953. Members only, but the club sets aside tee times for visitors, traditionally on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays. Ask the club.
courses.designer: C. B. Macdonald and Seth Raynor
sig: From a high tee you drive across Mangrove Lake and choose how much of the water to bite off. The braver the line, the shorter the second shot. It is the hardest hole on the card and one of the most copied holes in golf.
more: The 13th, a 238 yard par 3, plays to a Biarritz green, with a deep swale across its middle.
The 12th is a sharp dogleg left.
The 18th is a long par 4 that finishes along the ocean.

courses.name: Tucker's Point Golf Club
courses.kind: Hamilton Parish. 18 holes. Resort and private.
courses.what: Beside the Rosewood, on the hills above Castle Harbour. It began in 1932 as Charles Banks's Castle Harbour course and was rebuilt by Roger Rulewich in 2002. Hilly, with downhill drives and uphill, often blind, approaches.
courses.designer: Charles Banks, rebuilt by Roger Rulewich
sig: The 17th, par 4, 310 yards from the blue tees
A short par 4 from a high tee with Castle Harbour spread out below. Everybody stops to take the photograph.
more: The 11th, a par 3 of 210 yards, is often called the most scenic hole on the course.
The 6th, a 430 yard par 4, is rated the hardest hole.

card.note: The back Black tees stretch it to 6,491

courses.name: Belmont Hills Golf Club
courses.what: Short, tight and quirky, with tiered greens and views over Hamilton Harbour and the Great Sound. Devereux Emmet built the first course here in 1923 and Algie Pulley rebuilt it in 2002. Accuracy matters far more than length.
courses.designer: Devereux Emmet, rebuilt by Algie M. Pulley Jr.
sig: A drop shot from a high tee with the Great Sound laid out behind the green. The best view on the course.
more: The 2nd has one of the oddest, scariest tee shots anywhere.
Holes 1 and 10 share one wide, wandering double green.
The 15th, a 436 yard par 4, is rated the hardest hole.

courses.name: Turtle Hill Golf Club
courses.what: The par 3 course on the hill at the Fairmont Southampton, with ocean views and plenty of sand. Do not take it lightly: the holes run from 115 to 220 yards. It offers night golf and FootGolf.
sig: The longest hole on the course and one of the two hardest. Reviewers also single out the 17th, set inland, as possibly the best hole here.

courses.name: Five Forts Golf Club
courses.kind: St George's. 18 holes. Resort, open to the public.
courses.what: A short course at the St. Regis, reopened in 2021 on the old St George's course of Robert Trent Jones Sr. You start by Fort Victoria and finish beside Fort St Catherine, with the sea in view almost all the way. A round takes two and a half to three hours.
sig: The finishing hole runs down to Fort St Catherine and the ocean. Visitors call it the favourite.
more: The 1st, a 368 yard par 4, is rated the hardest hole.
Ten of the eighteen holes are par 3s.

courses.name: Ocean View Golf Course
courses.what: The relaxed, affordable one on the North Shore, with tight fairways, a few blind shots and a lot of up and down. Play the nine twice for a full round of 5,658 yards, par 70. It shares playing privileges with Port Royal.
courses.fee: $60 for 18 holes, $40 for nine or at sunset
sig: Rated the hardest hole on the card.

card.tee: White and blue tees, nine holes

sports.name: Dance
sports.lead: Latin nights on Front Street, adult classes you can drop into, and the island's dance schools.

sessions.what: Clave Dance: bachata, then salsa, then a social
sessions.where: Docksider, 121 Front Street, Hamilton
sessions.note: Bachata lesson at 7pm, salsa at 8pm and social dancing from 9pm. $12 a class. Beginners welcome. Listed weekly to 24 December 2026.

sessions.where: In Motion School of Dance, Studio 1

sessions.what: Adult ballet and jazz at In Motion
sessions.where: In Motion School of Dance, Studio 3

sessions.when: Through the week, September to June
sessions.what: Adult classes at Jackson's: tap, ballet, salsa and hip hop
sessions.where: Jackson's School of Performing Arts, 15 Burnaby Street, Hamilton
sessions.note: For ages 18 and over. $22 to drop in, $100 for a card of five, $200 for ten. The days and times are on the school's timetable.

bodies.name: Clave Dance Bermuda
bodies.what: The island's Latin dance community: salsa, bachata and more. It began as a Thursday social and marked ten years in July 2026 with a four day festival.

bodies.name: In Motion School of Dance
bodies.what: Four air conditioned studios and a dancewear shop. Ballet, pointe, tap, jazz and street style for children, teens and adults, from a parents and tots class on Saturday mornings up to its own company.

bodies.name: Jackson's School of Performing Arts
bodies.what: 15 Burnaby Street, Hamilton. Classes from age 2 to adult: creative dance, ballet, pointe, modern, contemporary, jazz, tap, hip hop, musical theatre and salsa, plus barre and Pilates.

bodies.name: DanceSations
bodies.what: 91 Reid Street, Hamilton. Ballet, pointe, modern, hip hop, jazz, tap and barre strength for children and adults. Call 292-4100 or see the school's schedule page.

bodies.name: Dance101 Bermuda
bodies.what: Chair dance classes for women aged 18 and over, running since 2015. Classes last 90 minutes, are beginner friendly, and every sixth one is free.

bodies.name: The Studio CLA
bodies.what: Children's classes in dance, music, cheerleading and gymnastics.

tips: The schools teach by term, usually September to June, and children's classes are grouped by age or grade. Each school's website has the full list.
Adult classes are the ones you can usually drop into. Ask before turning up to anything else.
sports.source_note: Class times from each studio's own website. Only adult and drop in classes are listed in full.

sports.name: CrossFit
sports.lead: Two boxes in and around Hamilton, with classes from six in the morning.

sessions.where: 8 Mills Creek, Pembroke
sessions.note: Your first workout is free. Book it on the website.

8 Mills Creek, Pembroke

sessions.what: CrossFit BDA: 9am class, then open gym
sessions.where: 8 Mills Creek, Pembroke

bodies.name: CrossFit BDA
bodies.what: 8 Mills Creek, Pembroke. Coached classes five times a day on weekdays. Call 535-4775.

bodies.name: LifeThyme CrossFit
bodies.what: 7 Dundonald Street West, Hamilton. Listed on CrossFit's own map of affiliated gyms, with twelve years as an affiliate. Tripadvisor lists it open from 6:15am on weekdays and 9am to 11am on Saturday, and visitors praise the coaching for drop ins. Check the times with the gym.

tips: Hyrox training is offered at Beyond Fit on Par-la-Ville Road. See Gyms and classes.

sessions.note: Its other classes run twice a week each. The gym gives the times on request.

bodies.name: Court House Squash and Wellness
bodies.what: Two clubs with 24 hour access, public holidays included: Central at 31 Victoria Street and West at 71 Pitts Bay Road. Yoga, Barre Burn, Pure Core Pilates and group cycling on 40 bikes, plus squash. The class timetable is in the club's booking system.

bodies.name: Magnum Power Force Gym
bodies.what: 70 Church Street East. 11,000 square feet over two floors with two class studios, a kids zone, sauna and steam. Staffed from 6:30am Monday to Wednesday, 7:30am Thursday and Friday, 9am at weekends, with 24 hour access for members. Call 292-7007.

bodies.name: Alchemy Fitness Studio
bodies.what: 22 Reid Street for classes, personal training and Reformer Pilates, open Monday to Saturday 6am to 7pm. 129 Front Street is a gym for training on your own, open 5am to 10pm every day. Classes include boxing, Muay Thai, mat Pilates, yoga and strength and conditioning. New members can buy one week of unlimited classes for $50.

bodies.name: Beyond Fit Bermuda
bodies.what: Mintflower Place, 8 Par-la-Ville Road. Open Monday to Saturday, 6am to 6:30pm. Sweat, a full body interval class, plus strength, Pilates and spin, and programmes for Hyrox and running. The timetable is in its booking calendar.

bodies.name: Fit4Life
bodies.what: 135 Front Street. Classes of about 45 minutes: full body conditioning, upper and lower body strength, and a sled session on Sundays. The first class is free. Call 261-0711.

bodies.name: The gym and spa at the Hamilton Princess
bodies.what: 76 Pitts Bay Road. Barre, cycle, yoga, cardio and interval classes in a studio overlooking the harbour, with memberships for residents that include unlimited classes. It was run for years as Exhale, and one guide says it has been renamed Driftwood Spa, so check the name and the timetable with the hotel.

tips: Three gyms keep their timetables inside booking systems the Hub cannot read yet: Court House, Alchemy and Beyond Fit. The buttons above open them.
Other hotels have gyms too, among them Rosewood, The Loren and Cambridge Beaches. The Hub found no public class timetable for them, so ask the hotel whether residents can join in.
Yoga has its own section, with live timetables for two studios.
